speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your scalp and forehead rash, can you describe exactly what it looks like and how long you've had it? Please also let me know if it is itchy, painful, or if you've noticed any hair loss in the affected areas.

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the diaper area, or is it primarily located on the scalp and face? Also, have you noticed any scaling or redness in the skin folds, such as behind the ears or in the neck crease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The greasy yellow scales and involvement of the scalp and forehead are classic signs of infantile seborrheic dermatitis. Given the patient's age and presentation, I am confident in my assessment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis
